title: Cumulative vs active pod restarts
one_line: A pod's restartCount is cumulative since creation, so a high count is not proof it is crashlooping right now.

worked_examples.context: kube_crashloop_pods shows high restart counts on several system pods after a node reboot.
steps: Read restartCount as cumulative since the pod was created, not as a live signal.
Check the last state and exit code - exit 0 with reason Completed is a benign finish, not a crash.
Compare the last restart timestamp to now - old timestamps mean historical, not active.
Flag only pods with recent, repeated restarts and a non-zero failing exit as actively broken.
worked_examples.result: Distinguish a pod that finished cleanly or restarted days ago from one looping now; recommend action only for the latter.

constraints.must: an 'actively broken' claim rests on recent repeated restarts plus a failing exit, not on the raw count alone
constraints.violated_feedback: You treated a high cumulative restartCount as an active crashloop; check recency and exit code first.

misconceptions.belief: a high restartCount always means the pod is crashlooping now
misconceptions.correction: restartCount accumulates over the pod's whole life; an exit-0 Completed pod or an old restart is benign.
